references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus expresses his amazement at the officer's faith and says he has not found such great faith in Israel.
Jesus praises the great faith of the Canaanite woman – yet another example of a Gentile showing remarkable faith that surpasses what Jesus finds in Israel.
Jesus marveled at the people's unbelief in Nazareth – a contrast to his amazement at the officer's faith in Luke 7:9.
Paul quotes Isaiah about God being found by those who did not seek him, pointing to the faith of Gentiles that surpasses that of Israel.
Paul speaks of Gentiles standing by faith while natural branches were broken off due to unbelief, reflecting the theme of faith outside Israel.
Jesus mentions the widow in Zarephath and Naaman the Syrian as examples of God showing grace to Gentiles rather than Israelites – the same theme of faith outside Israel.
Jesus asks whether he will find faith on earth when the Son of Man comes, reflecting his concern over the lack of faith in Israel.
The definition of faith as being sure of what we hope for and certain of what we do not see – the officer's faith in Luke 7 is a practical example of this definition.
